The Jammu and Kashmir Agriculture Production Department has received a proposal seeking transfer of more than 1,500 kanals of its land at Allowpora in Shopian to SKUAST-K for establishing a Centre of Excellence, with the proposal subsequently forwarded to the University for examination.
The issue was raised by MLA Shopian Shabir Ahmad Kullay through an Un-Starred Question in the Legislative Assembly, asking whether the government had received a proposal for utilisation/transfer of more than 1,100 kanals of land belonging to the Allowpora Seed Farm to SKUAST-K for establishment of a Centre of Excellence in Horticulture, including production of quality planting material, seed multiplication and seed development.
In its written reply, the Agriculture Production Department said it had received a D.O. communication from Kullay dated July 24, 2026, regarding the transfer of more than 1,500 kanals of Agriculture Department land at Allowpora to SKUAST-K for establishment of a Centre of Excellence for production of quality planting material.
“The proposal was received in the Agriculture Production Department and was forwarded to SKUAST-K for examination,” said the department.
According to the reply, SKUAST-K, in its communication dated August 19, 2026, proposed establishment of a Centre of Excellence for certified disease-free planting material, elite clonal rootstock multiplication and breeder/foundation seed production, besides diploma and short-term certificate courses, demonstration orchards, mother blocks, polyhouses and farmer-training facilities.
SKUAST-K has also proposed developing Allowpora as a regional scientific and skill hub for horticulture in South Kashmir, according to the reply.
However, in response to a separate question on whether a substantial portion of the farm was lying vacant or underutilised, the department said the 64.885-hectare farm was largely being utilised.
Of the total area, 58.90 hectares are presently being utilised for seed multiplication activities involving maize, oats, pulses, potato and floriculture seedlings, it said.
The department further said 20 hectares had been identified for establishment of a Saffron Corm Nursery, for which Rs 4.03 crore had been approved by the Government of India under PM-RKVY.
A Centre of Excellence for Precision Farming is also being established under the Capex Budget/SASCI scheme during the current financial year, with an allocation of Rs 4.96 crore, the reply said.
“In view of the above, it is not a fact that a substantial portion of the Seed Multiplication Farm, Allowpora is lying vacant or underutilized,” the department stated.
On whether the land would subsequently be transferred to SKUAST-K, the department said that since the land was already being utilised for various ongoing departmental activities, including seed multiplication, establishment of a Saffron Corm Nursery and a Centre of Excellence for Precision Farming, “transfer of the Allowpora Seed Farm land to SKUAST-K for the proposed purpose is not under consideration.”

The ASUS ProArt PZ14 is a powerful 2-in-1 Windows tablet for creators, with a sharp 3K OLED display, strong Snapdragon X2 Elite performance, excellent battery life, and full desktop apps. However, its high price, weak touch experience, and some ARM app limits hold it back.
People still debate why the tablet category exists. Some people believe they can replace laptops, while others see them as glorified smartphones with bigger screens.
I agree with both statements, as tablets are extremely portable. They are thinner, lighter, and easy to carry anywhere, and they can also convert into a laptop on the go, with the added advantage of a stylus for note-taking, sketching, or even marking up PDF files. Not to mention, they’re also great for watching movies and other entertainment.
But they are extremely limited in software capabilities despite hardware that can run fully native desktop applications. But Apple’s software limitations are also a deal-breaker for many. On the other hand, it runs the full Windows 11 OS on tablets without limitations. But it isn’t optimized for tablets.
For most people, or for creative work, the iPad is the first choice. But I recently got a chance to review the ASUS ProArt PZ14, which is a 2-in-1, tablet-first Windows device designed for creative work that is portable and offers an excellent OLED screen, solid performance, solid battery life, and is capable of running fully native applications, and comes with a keyboard and a pen out of the box for all your creative work and note-taking. I have been using the ASUS ProArt PZ14 for the past two weeks. In this detailed review, you will find out whether the ASUS ProArt PZ14 breaks tradition by doing things differently. Or is it just another tablet in the debate? Let’s find out.
Table of Contents
ASUS ProArt PZ14 Design and Build: Lightweight and practical, but the design is an acquired taste
ASUS ProArt PZ14 is a tablet-first Windows PC. The keyboard detaches completely from the tablet, and all components, including the processor, sit on the back of the display.
As a result, it carries all the weight. ASUS includes a magnetic case in the box that you can attach to the back of the tablet to use as a stand and to hold the ASUS Pen 3.0. I wouldn’t recommend attaching it without the case because, while you’re holding the tablet, the magnets are not strong, and it can easily fall off, which it did. But hopefully, thanks to the build, it survived accidental falls.
Thanks to the matte finish, the back of the tablet isn’t a fingerprint magnet either, but stains are visible if you look at it a certain way, and they wipe off easily with any standard cloth.
An ASUS design choice on the back can be a hit or a miss depending on your perception. Right off the bat, the ASUS ProArt PZ14 doesn’t look like a tablet. It felt like a very niche tablet designed for a specific purpose. It has a single rear camera. Thankfully, there is no bump, and it comes with a lot of stickers, which indicates it is more than just a tablet.
You get ProArt branding at the top in the center. Overall, the fit and finish are solid, but the looks can be hit or miss based on your perception. I wish it looked more like a tablet.
The ASUS ProArt PZ14 comes with dual speakers, with one on each side The power button is on the top in landscape and on the right in portrait, which is convenient for landscape use but less convenient in portrait.
And you can find the volume-down and volume-up keys on the right as well, making it easy to control with your right hand. The SD Express 7.0 card reader and two USB4 Type-C ports are on the left side.
The look changes entirely from the front. It comes with a 14-inch 3K OLED display with a 144Hz refresh rate and minimal bezels, similar to the iPad Pro, but wider overall. At the top, you get an 8MP IR front camera with no privacy shutter.
The tablet weighs just 790 grams, making it lightweight and easy to use, but the larger display is hard to hold for long periods when using it as a tablet. The tablet has rounded corners on the back, which make it easy to hold for long periods, and the textured finish on the front half provides better grip. The matte finish makes it less slippery.
The ASUS ProArt PZ14 also has an IP52 rating. ASUS officially claims that it is tested to MIL-STD-810Hstandards . So you have the military standard, but don’t drop-test it like other laptops.
When I first held the ASUS ProArt PZ14, the back finish felt like plastic. However, ASUS claims the chassis uses an aluminum alloy. The sides feel very solid.
ASUS ProArt PZ14 Display: A gorgeous 3K OLED made for creators
The ASUS ProArt PZ14 display is one of the best-looking, and if there is one reason to choose this tablet, it’s this display. Whether you are a business user, a graphic designer, or someone who wants to casually watch movies and play games, it delivers a great viewing experience.
The ASUS ProArt PZ14 comes with a 14-inch 3K OLED display. It comes with a 144Hz refresh rate for a smooth experience. The 14-inch display is a sweet spot. On your desk and used with the keyboard, it is a sweet spot and a perfect middle ground between the 13.6-inch and 15-inch laptops, but it feels very large in hand when you hold it and use it as a tablet.
The OLED display is one of the best I have seen on a tablet, matching premium, high-quality displays with 100% DCI-P3 color gamut and PANTONE validation. The blacks look deeper, and colors are represented very accurately, making it a good choice for designers and photographers who want to edit images accurately. The touch response is also fast, but Windows is the one to blame. It makes interactions less convenient, which I will cover more in the OS section.
The display also supports a stylus. ASUS includes the ASUS Pen 3.0 out of the box. Writing and drawing on the display feels faster and more fluid. But because of the glass finish, it feels slippery while taking notes. You can apply a matte-finish screen protector for a better typing and note-taking experience on this tablet. After the iPad Pro, the ASUS ProArt PZ14 provided the best note-taking experience, even better than the Apple Pencil in some cases.
ASUS, being extra generous, added the pencil-scribble sound while taking notes. Well, thank you, ASUS, for looking at those tiny details to enhance the user experience. But it sounds so artificial.
Next, this 16:10 aspect ratio is perfect for watching content. I watched three episodes of Better Call Saul (season 4) on Netflix, and the experience was better on the ASUS ProArt PZ14 than on my iPad Pro.
With 3K resolution and 243 pixels per inch, it is also one of the sharper displays. It looks sharp even when you zoom in on minor editing details.
However, if you often read web pages, blogs, or docs on this tablet, while it looks fine when using it in laptop mode, as soon as you pick it up and use it as a tablet, you are holding a massive tablet, and 16:10 feels very wide when you put it close to your eyes, which means you need to move your head to read the text. Also, portrait mode isn’t appealing either, with that 14-inch massive screen making it hard to read and scroll. With this large form factor, using it with a single hand is almost impossible. You can try if you want.
Overall, the display is one of the ASUS ProArt PZ14’s biggest strengths. Whether you’re watching content, editing, or designing, everything looks incredible on this massive screen.
ASUS ProArt PZ14 Keyboard and Trackpad: Laptop-like typing, but better suited for a desk
ASUS also provides a keyboard out of the box. Unlike with the iPads, which you need to buy separately and are also expensive. Fortunately, the typing experience is as good as on thin-and-light laptops. However, if you’re used to mechanical keyboards or longer key travel, you might find it hard to type at first, but you can eventually get used to it.
Also, there are a few things that you need to know: the keyboard completely detaches from the tablet, which means it doesn’t have a hinge that holds the display and keyboard together. A small magnetic attachment on the bottom of the tablet connects to the keyboard.
You can just hover the tablet over the keyboard, and it attaches magnetically. However, the magnet isn’t as strong, so it can also detach easily. And since there is no strong hinge holding the keyboard and tablet together, you cannot place it on your lap and type on uneven surfaces, where the tablet takes the full weight and could tip back.
Fortunately, ASUS also included a full touchpad, and again, it’s almost like using the touchpad on a regular thin-and-light laptop. The speakers are very loud. They have rich sound. There is no headphone jack.
ASUS ProArt PZ14 Specs and Performance: Snapdragon X2 Elite delivers plenty of power
Under the hood, the ASUS ProArt PZ14 runs on the Snapdragon X2 Elite X2E-88-100 processor. My variant has 32GB of LPDDR5X RAM and a 1TB M.2 NVMe PCIe 4.0 SSD. That’s a large configuration by current standards.
Qualcomm is trying too hard to become a name for its PC processors after it conquered Android phones. The processor offers very solid performance. Tasks feel faster, and it compares with some of the best in the industry right now, including the Intel Core Ultra 7 series and Ryzen AI Max+, among others. In comparison, in Geekbench single- and multicore scores, Snapdragon X2 Elite has produced very good numbers.
You can see the benchmarks of the ASUS ProART PZ14 from third-party testers.
The tablet also offers a dedicated performance mode that provides extra power when needed. This results in smooth day-to-day performance; whether it’s opening apps, touch interactions, gaming, or uploading files, everything feels smoother on this tablet
The built-in SD Express 7.0 card reader delivers strong sequential read and write rates, including 730 MB/s sequential read speeds. So if you are a creator who copies videos and files to and from the tablet, the ASUS ProArt PZ14 won’t consume your time.
However, while the processor is solid in CPU performance, the GPU is still weaker on Snapdragon processors, and the same is true of the Snapdragon X2 Elite. It comes with an integrated Qualcomm Adreno GPU. That performs decently; however, it’s not as good as Radeon or Intel Arc GPUs.
Because of this, it might not excel at higher-end applications or even gaming. It can offer decent performance, but not top-tier.
While the GPU might not be the most powerful, the NPU performance is significantly better. The Snapdragon X2 Elite includes a Qualcomm Hexagon NPU rated up to 80 TOPS. This lets you offload a few AI tasks locally for better performance. For instance, if you are a creator, you can run AI models locally.
ASUS ProArt PZ14 also comes with a fan. Under load, the tablet tends to get a bit warmer, and the fan kicks in.
Overall performance is impressive for such a thin and light device. Daily use, such as browsing the web, watching movies and shows, and running a few high-end software applications, feels faster and handles every task without breaking a sweat.
Moreover, while compatibility with popular ARM apps on Windows has improved over the years since Qualcomm announced Snapdragon X Elite, some older programs and plug-ins still aren’t natively compatible with Windows on ARM, and some run via x86 emulation.
ASUS ProArt PZ14 Battery Life: Easily lasts an entire workday
The battery life is incredible on this tablet, and Windows on ARM has already proved it. The ASUS ProArt PZ14 comes with a 75Wh four-cell lithium-ion battery. ASUS also offers a 68W USB-C charger in the box.
Even in performance and non-performance modes, battery life stays consistent. On average, I got around 12 to 14 hours of battery life with light to medium use and about 10-11 hours with heavy use, including gaming. With light use, just using the browser, I even got two days of battery life.
ASUS ProArt PZ14 Windows 11 Experience: Full desktop software, but a poor tablet interface
Now let’s address the elephant in the room: Windows 11. I would say having Windows 11 is both the biggest strength and also the biggest weakness of this tablet. The ASUS ProArt PZ14 ships with Windows 11 or Windows 11 Pro out of the box, depending on the configuration. My unit comes with Windows 11 Home.
No matter which version you are on, Windows 11 isn’t optimized for the touch interface. In Windows 11 touch mode, it feels like a desktop and has very small buttons, menus, and toolbars.
If you primarily want to use the ASUS ProArt PZ14 as a tablet, and you’re used to iPad Pro-type interaction, you will definitely find it hard to use day-to-day. Fortunately, using the pen minimizes this. However, if you primarily use your hands, keep that in mind.
Also, this tablet has a core Windows problem. The biggest problem is the annoying Windows updates. They are still an issue even after Microsoft promised to reduce those interruptions. Unfortunately, I haven’t been able to set up the tablet from scratch because it’s a pre-owned unit, and someone else has already set it up for me, so I was saved from dealing with lengthy setup processes.
Another big limitation of Windows running on ARM is limited app support. While app support has improved significantly since I first reviewed the Snapdragon X Elite laptop, most popular applications are now natively available on Windows on ARM, but a few legacy applications still use Prism emulation, which affects performance and misses core features. However, if you mainly want to use it as a creator tablet, most creator apps are natively available on Windows, and a few games are also natively supported on Windows on ARM.
But the biggest advantage is that, since it runs on Windows, you can run full desktop-level software without any limitations. You can multitask with multiple windows. If you want better multitasking and portability at the same time, this is something you should get.
ASUS ProArt PZ14 Ports and Connectivity: USB4 and SD Express are useful, but some ports are missing
Despite its tablet form factor, ASUS has included decent port support on the ASUS ProArt PZ14. It comes with two USB 4.0 Gen 3 Type-C ports that support up to 40 Gbps, which can be used to connect external SSDs, docks, and even an external monitor.
It also includes an SD Express 7.0 card reader, which is excellent for transferring video and photos from your cameras. There’s no HDMI port, which I miss, but you can easily work around it with external peripherals. The camera quality is also good, much better than the webcam quality on other ASUS laptops I have tested. The rear camera is also decent in good lighting, which you can use to scan documents quickly. The tablet also supports Wi-Fi 7 or Bluetooth 6.0.
ASUS ProArt PZ14 Verdict: A powerful Windows tablet for creators on the go
So, that is everything that you need to know about ASUS ProArt PZ14. With its excellent display, tablet-first design, portability, battery life, and solid performance, it is a great pick for anyone who wants a powerful tablet on the go.
The 3K OLED display also makes it a great option for entertainment whenever you want to watch content or even play games. Overall, the ASUS ProArt PZ14 is a great option for a creator-first experience and for anyone who values portability and wants an all-in-one tablet that can replace a conventional laptop and a tablet at home. However, the tablet costs Rs 2,69,990 for 32GB LPDDR5X RAM. It is expensive.

When the AI apocalypse becomes regular dinner-table conversation, you know we’ve reached the freakout stage. Rogue AI agents are hacking into competitors. Former Big Tech employees are posting Skynet-style warnings on social media. CEOs are crying for help in ways that have made this once-wonky tech issue a frontline political fight.
There’s a global plan to save humans from AI. Can it actually work?
Trump, Xi, and the UN are all talking AI this week. Here’s the question they need to answer.
I still think many of the concerns outlined by the AI leaders themselves are massively self-serving — especially when their companies are soon to go public. But the growing list of AI scandals is real. And it tells us that the status quo for regulating this powerful new technology is not working.
The question now on everyone’s mind: Is any kind of global brake possible? What form of AI safety regime is practical, over the short term, when there is no trust between major governments? And what could possibly work when companies are loath to give up their secret sauce and are bent on domination in the global AI race?
Two major conversations are now playing out, in real time. On Wednesday, President Donald Trump welcomed Chinese President Xi Jinping to Washington for a three-day summit — part of which will be dedicated to AI risks. The same day, with the United Nations meeting for its annual General Assembly, heads of the world’s leading AI companies urged the UN to police the emerging technology, or risk potentially wiping out humanity. “We could lose control of the future to AI,” OpenAI’s boss, Sam Altman, bluntly told the UN’s Security Council.
Confronted with this collective freakout, it’s time to take a long, deep breath.
In fact, AI safety has been on a lot of policymakers’ minds for years now, gaining momentum after ChatGPT was introduced in 2022. Governments have held hearings, convened expert groups, and drafted their own outlines of how to keep it under control. These weren’t just idle listening exercises. They aren’t all well known to the wider public, but they yielded real plans.
Barring any breakthroughs this week, we already have a quasi-planetary shield against the potentially runaway technology. That’s the good news.
The bad news is that it’s not really up and running yet. It’s also not clear whether it will actually work. So what is it — and how can we fix it so we have a global system that responds in time to deal with the incredibly fast-moving threats from AI?
What the global AI patchwork looks like now
For the last four years, the most tech-savvy nations — and would-be AI leaders — have been running serious conversations about this exact AI safety threat. Some are in Congress and the White House; some at the UN, at the G7, and in other capitals.
I’ve been covering this closely as a global technology journalist, from my current perch at a think tank. Here’s what the landscape looks like:
- There are national AI safety and security institutes, government-funded bodies whose job it is to kick the tires of AI companies’ latest products before they are let loose into the wild.
- There are also voluntary commitments by companies, many of which have made their own pledges or developed joint standards, to protect elections from AI threats, stop the spread of AI-fueled deepfake imagery, and joint government-corporate efforts to bake safety into how the technology develops.
- At the international level, there’s a G7-led reporting mechanism — embraced by the most important Western tech nations that allows AI giants to share how they are building their latest models, as well as create standards for how to reduce catastrophic risks.
- An international scientific report provides a yearly update on risks posed by the most advanced AI systems, based on existing research, to help governments plan for the worst.
What’s missing from all that? What we currently lack — and what is needed between now and the end of 2026 — is a way to turn this cottage industry of AI safety mechanisms into a functioning, but crude, first-responder system when things suddenly go wrong.
The last four years have laid out a pathway, and some of the necessary systems even exist. But there’s no way to respond globally, and in real time, when an AI crisis hits — especially if such a possibly doomsday event cuts across countries already skeptical of each other.
This week’s US-China summit may be a step in the right direction. Under proposals outlined by American officials, Washington and Beijing could set up a hotline between US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng in case of an AI incident affected each country’s national security.
It’s still unclear if Trump’s meeting with Xi will lead to such progress. Chinese officials also have balked at Washington’s pleas for AI rules because, so far, Congress has failed to act, and China already has some of the world’s most stringent AI oversight.
For AI to be “safe,” this conversation will need to go beyond this week’s US-China summit. Relying just on Washington and Beijing — arguably the most important AI powers — would not solve the underlying problems, nor would it make other countries feel more comfortable.
What we need next, so it really saves us
I’ve been talking to AI safety experts and government officials, and it’s clear the missing piece is a way to activate this whole system in a crisis. Countries don’t all have to have the same AI safety policies, and they never will. But as with nuclear weapons — a similarly high-threat technology that the world found a way to contain — safety requires a rough global agreement on how to respond quickly when something goes terribly wrong.
What’s needed right now is a 90-day, opt-in rapid response mechanism that joins existing pieces of the AI safety puzzle together. I’ve pieced together some ideas about how it should work, and who needs to sign on. Granted, none of what I outline below is sufficient. But, together, they are more plausible than trying to negotiate a comprehensive global regime — let alone arrange another AI summit — while Washington, Beijing, and other national capitals disagree over what “AI safety” actually means.
All of these options are based on existing mechanisms, are derived from efforts that have worked in other policy areas, and provide a band-aid to the AI safety dilemma until a more durable solution can be negotiated.
- First, developers, AI safety institutes, and regulators, from across different countries, should agree that when an incident occurs, it triggers a specific Chernobyl-style protocol. That would mean submitting a confidential report within a 72-hour period to a national designated responder and a small technical secretariat. It can build on the OECD’s AI Incidents Monitor, lead to a technical, multi-stakeholder confidential investigation into what went wrong, and, subsequently, the publication of an anonymized lessons-learned note.
- Second, governments and developers can agree to publish common declarations related to safeguards, residual risks, escalation thresholds, and independent auditing before the release or upgrading of a next-generation model. It would use the G7 Hiroshima AI Process reporting framework as its base, and turn the current hodgepodge of corporate safety declarations and voluntary standards into a common minimum disclosure obligation. View it as similar to the collective bank stress tests after the 2008 global financial crisis. It can allow outsiders to truly compare models’ safety protocols without putting someone in charge of determining which company is doing it best.
- Third, create a Cold War-style US-China AI safety hotline — but see it as an initial step that can later be opened to other countries. There are good reasons, in the long term, that Washington and Beijing should not be allowed to rule artificial intelligence between them, and the rest of the world should have a real seat at the table. But for now those are the two “great powers” in the tech conversation, and we can set that philosophical argument aside to create a standing, technically-informed direct line of communication for acute AI-risk incidents. Its remit is inherently narrow: prevent dangerous misunderstandings linked to serious model incidents, AI-enabled cyberattacks and/or alleged breaches of agreed safety commitments.
There are obvious limits to what I describe above. For one, it’s an inherently Western-centric view that primarily discounts global majority countries. It also places too much sway on existing institutions like the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development, as well as on the US-China relationship. Other countries’ officials will legitimately balk at all three options, and rightly so.
But this is not about creating a vague, unenforceable UN-led mandate for AI safety. Nor is it about corralling the geopolitical cats to hammer out a global AI treaty. The options — a collective safety protocol and incident reporting protocol; common pre-release standards; and a US-China AI safety hotline — are inherently short-term. They are also based on existing efforts and those that have worked successfully for other policy areas.
There will be time to quibble about the future of AI safety. But now is not that time. The latest AI models are moving faster than many had expected, tech bosses are worried their creations are already out of control, and the window for action may be smaller than we all think.
What is required are practical steps to assuage people’s growing concerns amid heightened geopolitical tension, a lack of trust between governments and companies, and a need not to let the perfect get in the way of the good.

Gemini Live vs. ChatGPT Voice: Which AI offers a more natural conversation?
It's actually too natural for some.
When ChatGPT first launched in 2022, the only way to interact with it was through your keyboard. But it didn't take long for another breakthrough: real-time voice chat. ChatGPT's Voice Mode was the first feature of this kind, but we soon got competition from Google in the form of Gemini Live as well. Unlike older voice assistants like the Google Assistant, these chatbots can hold natural conversations on just about any subject and even search the internet for up-to-date information.
Even so, Google and OpenAI have taken noticeably different approaches to voice chat with their respective chatbots. One has a slight edge in how natural it sounds, while the other modulates its responses based on information from your digital life. I've used both ChatGPT Voice and Gemini Live over the past couple of years; here's which one I reach for more often and why.
ChatGPT Voice vs. Gemini Live: Which is better?
On paper, ChatGPT Voice and Gemini Live share many similarities — both respond in real time and offer various voices to choose from. The primary difference lies in which underlying AI models they use: ChatGPT uses the GPT family while Google's chatbot uses Gemini. Theory aside, though, the real-world experience of using the two chatbots is quite different.
ChatGPT Voice tends to be much more expressive in its word selection and uses natural conversational markers in an attempt to sound more human. For example, it often pretends to think with a "mhmm" and even adds mid-sentence stutters.
Gemini Live's response often sounds flatter in its delivery, simply because of the differences in tone and inflection. Some people dislike ChatGPT's exaggerated intonations, though, so you may prefer Google's approach.
Another difference I noticed was that ChatGPT Voice is more likely to search for information on the internet before answering. When I asked both chatbots about the recent Gemini 3.8 Live release, Gemini defaulted to its existing knowledge and proclaimed that it did not exist. ChatGPT Voice paused for a couple of seconds while it accessed the internet, but ultimately gave me the correct answer. In my experience, you often have to explicitly ask Gemini Live to research before responding if you value factual accuracy.
Other than these differences, though, both Gemini Live and ChatGPT Voice can answer questions, look up information and even switch between multiple languages on the fly. That said, don't expect the same quality of responses as you'd get from either chatbot's text mode. Since voice-based conversations require quick responses, both chatbots use slightly less capable models that prioritize speed over accuracy.
Are ChatGPT Voice and Gemini Live both free to use?
If you haven't paid for ChatGPT or Gemini, you'll quickly find that both chatbots only offer a few minutes of conversation before cutting access. This is because voice processing is significantly more computationally demanding than text alone. Both OpenAI and Google offer paid plans that greatly increase this limit and grant access to more capable AI models as well. On ChatGPT, for instance, I've noticed the GPT-Live-1 mini model on the free tier lacks the reasoning skills of the larger GPT-Live-1 model.
ChatGPT Go, the most affordable paid plan, will set you back $8 a month, while Google's AI Plus subscription costs $5 monthly. The next step up for both chatbots is $20 per month. I prefer Google's subscription options, as even the lowest tier bundles 400GB of cloud storage. The latter can also be shared with up to five family members.
As an aside, both chatbots support camera input alongside voice, allowing you to point your phone at your surroundings for added context. I often use this feature to show the AI what I'm working on instead of describing the task with words alone. I've used Gemini Live while tuning up my bike, for example, and the AI was able to walk me through the process. It even overlaid helpful markers on the live video feed so I could quickly identify which screws I needed to tighten.
Unfortunately, ChatGPT's camera access during voice chat is locked behind the chatbot's $20 monthly subscription tier. Google's equivalent feature is free, at least up to a certain limit. The entry-level ChatGPT Go subscription also surprisingly lacks camera access during voice chat — you'll need the $20 tier for that feature.
Gemini Live outshines ChatGPT Voice in some areas
Google's breadth of hardware and software services means that it has a natural advantage over OpenAI. Case in point: you can use Gemini Live on a dedicated smart speaker via a Google Home Speaker. In fact, the company even brought the feature to older Nest Audio and Hub devices. My Google Home Mini supports the feature too, which is impressive for a device launched in 2017. The only caveat is that you need an active Google Home Premium subscription ($10 per month) to use Gemini Live on smart home devices.
The Pixel Buds line also has deep Gemini Live integration, which allows you to start a conversation using just your voice. OpenAI is working on its own smart home hardware, but we haven't heard about pricing or availability just yet. Either way, Google has already sold millions of smart speakers and displays, so the cost of entry into the Gemini Live ecosystem is lower for many.
Gemini Live can also reference information from your personal Google account for more personalized responses. This feature, dubbed Personal Intelligence, can look up emails, YouTube videos, and documents saved to your Drive.
When I asked Gemini Live whether I received any bills this month, for example, it listed everything it found in my Gmail inbox after a few seconds of processing. Google's chatbot can also add a calendar event mid-conversation and control smart home devices. ChatGPT cannot peer into your digital life at this time, nor can it access Google's services like Maps and YouTube.
When I don't need any of these features, though, I often find myself reaching for ChatGPT Voice rather than Gemini Live simply because the former sounds more natural to my ears. Since both are available for free, I'd recommend testing them before paying for higher usage limits.

George Russell: Is Mercedes driver really back after 'Grand Slam' Azerbaijan GP win cut Kimi Antonelli's F1 title lead?

George Russell produced the most statistically complete weekend of his Formula 1 career to win the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, but did the performance confirm the Brit is back to his best?
Russell drove superbly in Baku to claim the first Grand Slam of his career, taking pole position, leading from lights-to-flag on his way to victory, and setting the fastest lap of the race.
The result saw Russell reduce his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli's lead at the top of the world championship to 66 points with eight rounds remaining, ensuring some intrigue remains as the season enters its closing stretch.

Regardless of whether Russell is able to mount a challenge over the remainder of the season, the gulf between him and Antonelli in recent months had begun to create doubts over the 28-year-old's prospects of ever winning a championship while driving alongside the Italian.
There were extenuating circumstances for Antonelli in Baku as he missed a significant chunk of practice with technical issues before crashing out of qualifying to leave himself 16th on the grid, but this was the first time since the opening weekend of the season that Russell had so clearly outperformed him.
Russell has been open in recent months about his difficulty understanding his deficit to Antonelli, which he has largely attributed to the different challenges posed by F1's new cars for 2026, but feels his Baku display was confirmation that a corner has been turned.
Russell said: "I think it's probably my first Grand Slam in Formula 1 and, for sure, the most dominant weekend I've had in my career, so that has come at a really great moment.
"And also to achieve it on a circuit that requires so much commitment and confidence, I'm really proud of because I think it would have been very easy for me to lose the faith this season. Not necessarily about winning the championship, but in terms of my ability, and that never happened.
"I'm very proud of the resilience that I and my close group of engineers have shown during the tough periods this year because there's been a lot of hard work to overcome some of the challenges, to adapt my driving style to suit this new car better.
"And F1 is so tough, you don't get opportunities to practice this, and finally it's coming to me a bit more intuitively than it once did, and I'm gaining confidence."
'He definitely stepped up'
Russell's victory was made all the more impressive by the fact he had to fend off Red Bull's Max Verstappen in the closing stages having had a big lead taken away by two Safety Car interruptions.
A thrilling race to the chequered flag saw Russell end up just a tenth of a second clear of Verstappen, creating the smallest margin of victory in an F1 race since 2002.
Three-time W Series champion and Sky Sports F1 pundit Jamie Chadwick believes the performance was confirmation that Russell has raised his level.
"He's definitely stepped up," Chadwick said.
"It's a big points gap but I think the championship is still something to be excited about, which for a lot of us coming into this weekend maybe we didn't expect. So that's something to look forward to now."
Sky Sports F1's Karun Chandhok was particularly impressed by the way Russell fended off four-time world champion Verstappen in the closing stages.

If Russell really has returned to form, it was good time to do so, with the Azerbaijan Grand Prix having been the first of six races in seven weeks.
The Bahrain Grand Prix, taking place in Malaysia, follows next weekend, with the Singapore Grand Prix completing a triple-header. Then come back-to-back races in the United States, Mexico and Brazil.
The fact Russell needs to take a grid penalty before the end of the season for changing engine stiffens his task, but just proving that he can match Antonelli for pace over the remainder of the year would be a huge psychological boost going into 2027.
Having rarely spoken with any great confidence in recent months, Russell's view on how he sees the battle between himself and Antonelli going forward suggests he has his mojo back.
"There's much less pressure on me than there is him," Russell said. "He's had an incredibly flawless season. Yesterday was probably his first mistake of this whole season in a proper session, qualifying, race, and he still came home in P5 today.
"I didn't really consider myself in this fight for a number of races, purely because my performance wasn't strong enough.
"Now I feel like if the season were to have started today, or since the summer break, I feel very much I would have been able to fight.
"Now I've got this big deficit. It can change quickly. So, I'm not chasing that. I'm chasing to win every race, and what will be, will be."

iOS 27 focuses on useful refinements, with better Liquid Glass controls, smarter Siri AI, natural-language Shortcuts, Safari web-change alerts, separate alarm volume, improved Photos tools, AirPods EQ, smarter password handling, and several everyday quality-of-life upgrades.
Apple has finally started rolling out iOS 27 to all eligible devices after testing it in beta for months. If you are reading this article, the update is already rolling out. If your iPhone supports it, you can go to Settings, General, Software Update, and update to the latest version.
iOS 27 isn’t a significant jump from what we have seen from iOS 18 to iOS 26. For those who are not aware, Apple has changed the version names to match the year. So instead of iOS 19, they moved it to iOS 26 to match the year 2026.
This year’s iOS 27 is more about refinement and fixing the issues that came along with iOS 26.
One of the biggest updates for most people, at least based on our insight, is the ability to refine the liquid glass design. Apple is now offering a separate setting to make your liquid glass look more frosted or transparent, and also allowing you to set different volumes for the alarms.
Plus, there is a new Siri and plenty of other Siri AI features, such as creating your own shortcuts using natural prompts. Let your password app fix compromised passwords, monitor website changes for free using Safari, and much more.
I have been testing iOS 27 for a few months now, testing its wide variety of features. In this guide, you will learn about the 27 best iOS 27 features that everybody should know and use for a better quality of life.
Table of Contents
Best iOS 27 Features You Should Know and Use
There are tens of new feature additions and improvements in iOS 27. However, not every new feature deserves your attention. There are a few features that really stood out for me and are genuinely useful in day-to-day life that everyone should be aware of. So here are my ten favorite picks before going to the comprehensive list of features.
Adjust Liquid Glass Design Transparency
It is evident that most people hated the new liquid glass design Apple introduced in iOS 26. Apple made the entire UI transparent overnight with a glossy effect, which made text hard to read and was resource-heavy.
Additionally, a few apps failed to adapt to this design perfectly, resulting in a bad user experience. However, Apple didn’t back off from the decision. Since the launch, Apple has continued to refine the liquid glass design to make it better and more usable.
In the latest iOS 27 update, Apple is offering a separate setting that lets you adjust the transparency of the liquid glass design. This setting is different from what we have covered in our TechPP videos, and here is how to use it.
Build Your Own Shortcuts Using Natural Prompts
Extensions and shortcuts are the two easiest ways to add missing features, whether it’s on your iPhone or in any browser. However, creating shortcuts isn’t always an easy task. It involves dealing with plenty of elements and actions, which can be hard for a casual user.
But that’s changing with iOS 27. The new Siri AI will now let you create a new shortcut based on simple, natural prompts. Now you can simply describe a shortcut using natural language, highlighting what it can do. For instance: A shortcut that automatically changes your iPhone wallpaper every morning or a shortcut that reminds you to drink water every two hours.
Since it uses AI behind the scenes, the possibilities are endless. You can describe whatever problem or feature you want to add through the shortcuts, and it will do it for you. However, the current implementation is not reliable for complex extensions. But it is a good start, and it will only get better in future versions.
I found using Claude or Codex to create iPhone shortcuts is the most reliable way, and it works much better for me than using Siri to create shortcuts, which often don’t get the desired results I wanted.
Let Your Password Apps Handle Your Compromised Passwords
When Apple first introduced the Passcodes app in iOS 18, it was super basic and missed a lot of the features found on other passcode management apps at the time. However, Apple continues to add new features, and the recent iOS 27 brings the ability to fix your compromised passwords automatically.
In simple words, if any of your passwords are compromised, your password app will automatically renew them into new passwords without you having to do it manually.
Password management apps are very good at finding your compromised passwords in data breaches. However, previously you had to manually visit every site and change the password yourself. But that’s going to change with iOS 27, where you can simply tap to auto-change the password, and it does it for you.
Monitor Any Web Changes in Real Time
This is my favorite addition to the Safari browser. Probably a feature that can kill many third-party apps. Apple has added a new Notify Me feature to the Safari web browser in iOS 27. It lets Siri AI monitor real-time changes on the website and notify you. Whether it’s an e-commerce price drop, real-time stock changes, or even a new article addition to any webpage, Safari can monitor it for you.
The best part is, you can describe what changes you want to get notified about in a natural prompt, and it does it for you. Also, there are no hard limits on how many trackers or websites you can track, and it lets you track changes every hour. Weekly, monthly, or even daily. The only requirement is that your device should support the Apple Intelligence feature.
Set Separate Volume for Your Alarms
Another feature that Apple should have introduced years ago is the ability to set custom volumes for your alarms in iOS 27. Previously, Apple used to have a single volume for all sounds, including alarms, calls, media, and notifications. In iOS 27, Apple is splitting that up, letting you set separate volume levels for alarms, media, and notifications.
One-Tap Access for Your Wi-Fi and Mobile Data Toggles
If you are someone who frequently adjusts the mobile and Wi-Fi toggles on your iPhone, iOS 27 is getting a very big, useful upgrade. Now, without needing to open the toggle or the entire panel, you can just individually turn your Wi-Fi toggle on and off directly from the toggle. It is enabled by default.
If you have customized it, you can just drag and drop the new network panel to get access to these features.
Auto-Paste Suggestions on Top of Your Keyboard
Another feature that Android users have enjoyed for years is now finally available on iPhone starting with iOS 27. Once you copy text or take a screenshot, the iOS keyboard now automatically suggests the recently copied clipboard text and images, which you can simply tap on and paste wherever you want.
Previously, it required you to long-press, select, and tap on the paste option to do that.
New Custom Equalizer for Your AirPods
Apple is rolling out a custom equalizer in the settings for AirPods. Now, iPhones with iOS 27 have a native AirPods equalizer in Settings to help you customize the audio output.
The new custom equalizer allows you to adjust lows, mids, and high frequencies separately. However, it is only available for devices running on H2 or later Pro devices, and for older devices, users need to rely on Apple’s Adaptive EQ.
Quickly View Photos Captured by You
One of the biggest downsides of iOS Photos is that the images captured from your iPhone are mixed with screenshots, memes, and other downloaded images saved from third-party apps. This makes it extremely hard for you to find the photos captured particularly from your iPhone. In iOS 27, Apple has added a new “Captured by Me” folder to the Photos app. It only shows the photos and videos taken with your iPhone camera, letting you easily find them.
Let Your Earbuds Automatically Pause When They Detect You Have Fallen Asleep
If you use AirPods, Apple has added another useful feature in iOS 27: your AirPods can automatically pause music, podcasts, or whatever you are listening to when they detect that you have fallen asleep.
Most apps these days offer sleep timers that automatically pause after a certain time. However, Apple’s implementation is more dynamic and doesn’t rely on a set time limit. Based on your movement, the AirPods automatically detect when you have fallen asleep and pause the music. This can be extra useful if you are someone like me who falls asleep, and it also eliminates the need for you to set a sleep timer every night.
The Phone App Automatically Shows Relevant Information While You Are on the Call
How many times have you searched for specific information during a call with a service agent? If your answer is often, then Apple has added a very useful feature for you.
With iOS 27, the Phone app on your iPhone now automatically shows relevant information when you are on a call in real time. These include your reservation numbers, order details, confirmation codes, and much more, which Apple can fetch from other Apple services. This eliminates the need for you to search through emails, messages, or other apps while speaking to customer support or during a business call.
Apple’s Mail App Is Now Better at Finding Information
If you use Apple Mail, it is getting a useful update. Starting with iOS 27, Apple says Mail search is upgraded to find more relevant information based on your search.
Now, instead of remembering the exact subject lines, names, or even words in your email, you can just use your natural tone and search for the exact information you want. Apple says the Mail app can now display more relevant information at the top of the search results, and it’s also smarter, as it can automatically identify the query and find the relevant information.
Now, You Can Set an Exact Expiry Time for Your Find My Sharing
If you use Apple’s Find My for location sharing, it is getting a useful update. You can select the exact time when your location sharing should stop. Previously, Apple only allowed you to share your location for an hour, until the end of the day, or until you manually turn it off.
But with iOS 27, Apple is giving you more flexibility, letting you choose a custom time. Now you can set a combination of days along with the hours to share your location. This also eliminates the need for you to manually remember to turn off location sharing if you have set it to indefinitely.
Now, You Can Turn Your Physical Cards Into Digital Passes
Apple Wallet app in iOS 27 lets you convert your physical cards into digital cards and store them in your Apple Wallet. Carrying a physical card can be a hassle, especially if you have multiple cards. It not only makes your wallet bulky, but also makes it hard to find the right one when you need it.
Moreover, there is a high chance that you can forget it, and it could get lost. Now, with the ability to convert your physical cards into digital ones, the Apple Wallet app eliminates all of these pain points. Plus, even if you want to carry a physical card, I would highly suggest converting it into a digital one, which can come in handy sometimes.
Improved AI Writing Tools Across the System
AI writing tools were the first Apple Intelligence features Apple introduced in iOS 18. However, Apple left them out and forgot to update them in iOS 26.
But in iOS 27, with the overall improvements in the AI features and getting close to what it has promised, Apple has also upgraded AI writing tools throughout the system.
Now, these writing tools are more advanced and improved. The best part of these AI writing tools is that they are integrated directly into the workflow.
So if you want to summarize, shorten, or fix spelling mistakes, you don’t need to switch apps. You can generate, rewrite, or correct text directly from your iPhone keyboard. Plus, Apple is also integrating these AI capabilities across the system, including Mail and the Notes app, letting you easily access them anywhere.
Easily Create Calendar Events Without Specific Details
Creating a calendar event requires you to fill in separate details for title, date, time, location, and other details. However, with iOS 27, Apple is making it easy for you to create or edit calendar events.
Now, without needing to fill everything manually, you can just create a calendar event using natural prompts.
For instance, you can ask Calendar to create a birthday event at 4 a.m. tomorrow, and it will do it for you. Calendar app can now understand details such as important keywords, dates (such as tomorrow at 4 PM), a person’s name, and other key details, and automatically create a calendar event. Plus, you can also edit using natural language.
Connect an iPhone Directly to Gym Equipment
If you own an iPhone and want to track your workout data, pairing it with an Apple Watch is the most sensible decision. However, it is expensive and can be overkill for users looking for basic fitness tracking features who don’t need distraction on their wrist.
However, the Apple Watch has this nifty feature where they connect to your gym equipment and receives live workout data, such as your speed, distance, pace, resistance, and the duration of your workout, which you can then measure and analyze in your Apple Health app.
If you do not own an Apple Watch or don’t want to carry it during your workout, Apple in iOS 27 has added the same GymKit functionality directly on your iPhone. So now your iPhone can directly connect to your compatible gym equipment and receive the live workout data. Plus, if you have an Acura Pro 3, you can also connect and track your real-time heart rate information.
Pause Location Sharing Without Disabling It Permanently
If you use Find My to share your location with others, iOS 27 is adding the ability to temporarily hide your location without permanently ending location sharing completely.
In previous versions, if you wanted to temporarily stop sharing your location, whether it’s because your iPhone battery is running out, or if you are planning a surprise, or if you don’t want to reveal your destination, you needed to permanently stop location sharing.
With iOS 27, you can temporarily hide your location from a person. The best part is that the person does not need to be removed, and you also do not need to remember to turn the location back on after the situation has ended.
New Improved Cleanup Tool for Your Photos
I personally hate AI photo editing features inside the Photos app. Recently, both Apple and Google have added several features that are designed to alter and convert your photos into AI-generated ones. However, one feature that I found very useful is the ability to remove unwanted people or objects from a photo directly in the Photos app without relying on third-party tools.
However, Apple’s initial version of the Clean Up Tool isn’t as great as expected. It struggled to remove unwanted distractions from an image. However, with iOS 27, Apple has significantly improved it. Now it’s on par with other clean-up tools that perfectly edit the image naturally, without leaving smudges or empty patches.
Automatically Organize Safari Tabs by Subject
With iOS 27, Apple’s Safari browser can now automatically organize tabs for you. Many other browsers have adopted this feature, but it took some time for Apple to implement it.
If you use the Safari browser and have many tabs open, you can enable the Auto-Organize feature so that it automatically organizes your tabs. This lets you easily find them or close all of them at once.
Generate Your Own Extensions for Safari
Similar to iOS Shortcuts, you can also generate your own extensions using natural prompts in Safari. If you have an Apple Intelligence-supported iPhone, you can just visit the extension tab and give it a natural prompt about what exact features the extension might have, and Apple Intelligence will create a fully working extension for you.
You can just use this extension for an individual web page, or for all the web pages in your Safari browser.
New Siri for Agentic Tasks
Apple is finally close to delivering the Siri it promised two years ago. With iOS 27, Apple is introducing the new Siri, called Siri AI, which is now better at answering your questions and also better at agentic tasks. Plus, it can now search across your Apple apps, including Mail, Messages, Photos, Notes, and all other supported apps, and get information for you.
You can create a reminder, edit a message, organize details, or complete another task. Plus, Siri can also have better context, which means it can remember the information that it gets from other apps. Although at its current stage it is not as advanced as Gemini or other intelligent or agentic AI tools, it is a good start for Apple to deliver what it promised.
It will only get better from now on. Plus, Siri is directly integrated into the system. You can activate it from any screen. Plus, it is free to use without any limitations, except for a few features that Apple might put behind a subscription paywall in the future.
New Wallpaper Extensions
If you customize your iPhone and set a new wallpaper often, this can come in handy. Apple is introducing a new wallpaper extension feature in iOS 27, which expands your wallpaper so it fits correctly based on your iPhone dimensions.
In most cases, if your iPhone wallpaper doesn’t match your iPhone screen dimensions, it can look blurry and pixelated. Plus, if you want to set it as a lock screen wallpaper, it can also affect the depth effect, making the overall wallpaper look blurry and clumsy.
With this new extension wallpaper, Apple now extends the wallpaper to perfectly fit your iPhone’s aspect ratio. The best part is it preserves the main subject and only generates the matching scenery at the image’s edges, so that the subject stays in the middle without being cut off.
Reply Inline to the Messages From Android Users
With the iOS 27 update, Apple is putting an end to another discussion of blue and green bubbles and Apple’s tactics to limit RCS messaging.
Apple iMessage now supports inline replies, where you can directly reply to a specific message sent from your Android friend. This is like a nested reply where you can long-press on any message and tap on Reply. Along with your reply, the other person’s message appears on top, making it easy for them to spot and understand.
New Siri Visual Intelligence
Siri is also now upgraded with better visual intelligence, and it is now live inside your camera app. Now you can spot objects inside your camera and ask Siri to describe them. This can be especially useful for visual intelligence tasks, such as translating the text from a photo, identifying a specific object or food, or extracting the details from a flyer.
Plus, the best part is that, since it is being done by Siri, you can also ask follow-up questions and even delegate tasks, such as adding the extracted information to your calendar or splitting and storing it in any app. Now, adjust your lock screen clock to make it look smaller.
This can be small, but useful for people who often customize their lock screen.
Apple is now letting you adjust the clock size on your iPhone lock screen. Now you can adjust the size of the lock screen clock even smaller. If you feel your clock is covering the important details of your wallpaper, or if you want it to take up less space, you can simply use the smaller clock feature to adjust its size and make it look smaller.
Organize Your Photos Better
While Apple’s Photos app search is smart enough to find the relevant image you are looking for using just natural prompts, Apple is also letting you add individual star ratings and keywords to the photos. Starting with iOS 27, you can rate the photos up to 5 stars and add keywords.
Photos app displays these details while you are browsing your media library, letting these photos stand out from the rest. This makes them easy to spot instead of manually comparing photos to find the best ones from your extensive media library.
Save Photos Directly From Videos
With iOS 27, Apple also introduced the ability to save any frame from a video. You can simply use the Save frame as a photo feature, and the video frame will be saved as a photo. You can save multiple frames as photos.
Here is how:
- Open the Photos app on your Phone
- Play any video and tap on the three-dot menu at the top
- From here, tap on the Save Video frame as a photo option
Get the Most Out of iOS 27
Those are the 27 best iOS 27 features that everyone should know and use.
Apple has officially started rolling out iOS 27. By the time we publish this post, the update is available for all eligible phones. You can update and test out these new features. Detailed videos of how to use the features are coming soon on our TechPP YouTube channel. If you have any issues or if you don’t find this feature on your iPhone, you can comment below. Srinagar, Sep 22: On the occasion of the annual Urs Mubarak of Hazrat Sheikh Syed Abdul Qadir Jilani (RA), Mirwaiz-e-Kashmir Dr. Moulvi Mohammad Umar Farooq delivered a special religious address at the historic Aastan-e-AaliyaDastgeer Sahib (RA), Khanyar, Srinagar.
As per a statement, a large number of devotees attended the spiritually uplifting gathering, including a significant number of women.
In his address, Mirwaiz dwelt upon the fundamental message of Tawheed — the absolute Oneness of Allah Almighty — and highlighted the timeless teachings and spiritual legacy of Hazrat Sheikh Syed Abdul Qadir Jilani (RA).
He said that Hazrat Sheikh Abdul Qadir Jilani (RA) consistently called upon believers to remain firmly attached to the Qur’an and Sunnah, purify their hearts and souls, perform righteous deeds, and place complete trust and reliance in Allah Almighty.
Mirwaiz said that at a time when Muslims across the world are passing through severe challenges, uncertainty and difficult circumstances, the teachings of the revered saint assume even greater relevance. He urged Muslims to strengthen their relationship with Allah Almighty through sincere prayer, genuine repentance, patience, steadfastness, firm faith and unwavering trust in Him.
He emphasised that closeness to Allah must also be reflected in one’s conduct towards fellow human beings, and urged the faithful to imbibe the values of humility, compassion, self-purification, righteous character and service to humanity that formed an integral part of the teachings of Hazrat Sheikh Syed Abdul Qadir Jilani (RA).
Mirwaiz stressed that true spirituality lies in sincere devotion to Allah, adherence to His commandments and following the path shown by the Holy Prophet Muhammad (SAW).
At the conclusion of his sermon and religious discourse, Mirwaiz recited a Manqabat in praise of Hazrat Peeran-e-Peer Sheikh Syed Abdul Qadir Jilani (RA) and paid rich tribute to his enduring religious, spiritual and reformative services to the Muslim Ummah.
Earlier, upon his arrival at Khanyar, Mirwaiz was accorded a warm and enthusiastic welcome by the people.

ACT's top cop supports anti-consorting laws amid police's battle against bikies
In short:
The ACT's chief police officer is publicly backing anti-consorting laws.
The laws are in place in most other Australian jurisdictions, but Labor-led ACT governments have argued they conflict with the Human Rights Act.
Police and experts argue now is the time to introduce the laws in the territory.
ACT Chief Police Officer Scott Lee has no doubt about the damage outlaw bikie gangs are causing in Canberra.
"Outlaw motorcycle gangs exist for one reason, and that's in relation to organised crime"
While raw numbers in the Canberra region do not match those in Sydney and Melbourne, there has been a notable increase in the past few years.
Deputy Commissioner Lee said there were currently five outlaw motorcycle gangs (OMCGs) in the ACT, with about 45 members and approximately 20 associates.
"So that number has grown, which is a concern for us," he said.
ACT Policing is stepping up its fight against this growing threat in a bid to disrupt the gangs' criminal activities.
Land of opportunity?
For decades the ACT had one established bikie gang that ruled the roost — the Rebels.
But since the early 2010s, most Rebels have "patched over" to other groups, including the Bandidos, the Hells Angels, the Finks, and the Comancheros.
Several now have established "chapters" or bases in the ACT, rather than using Canberra solely as a transit corridor.
Deputy Commissioner Lee thinks the primary reason is that Canberra is a growing city, and market.
"Where you have those prosperous communities, they're attractive propositions for investment, but they're also attractive propositions for crime," he said.
Associate Professor Mark Lauchs has been researching OMCG activities in Australia for decades.
"They're increasing in Canberra, because it's much harder for them to operate elsewhere in the country," he said.
Anti-consorting laws
One measure Deputy Commissioner Lee advocates for is anti-consorting laws, which have been a controversial debate in the ACT.
"We support that legislation," he said.
"We've seen the benefits of it in other jurisdictions where it has an ability to disrupt associations, or certainly overt associations, and the ability for these people to gather."
Deputy Commissioner Lee emphasised that anti-consorting laws preventing outlaw motorcycle gangs from meeting in public were not a magical cure-all.
"OMCGs continue to exist in every jurisdiction," he said.
"But where you have those real overt showings of OMCGs, what we have with the national runs, it would disrupt that type of activity."
The ACT has repeatedly resisted introducing these laws, with previous Labor-led governments arguing they conflict with the ACT Human Rights Act.
Associate Professor Lauchs agreed that "good, strong, well-targeted" anti-consorting laws were needed, but he said it was reasonable the ACT had resisted until now.
"The arguments [against anti-consorting laws] aren't wrong. There are human rights issues there that have to be addressed," he said.
"However, being right is not enough in this case, because everybody else did it.
"So, you became the eventual inevitable victim of everybody else's laws."
An attractive market
Sergeant Mark Alexander leads the specialist ongoing Task Force Invidia, which investigates, infiltrates and disrupts the gangs.
He said the groups were "really sophisticated, and their operational security is quite a challenge for us to try and monitor".
"They are an undercurrent and a really strong presence in the ACT in illicit commodities,"
Those commodities include the usual suspects — drugs, guns, weapons and extortion.
Associate Professor Lauchs argued that the illicit drug trade was the big draw for outlaw gangs.
"Is Canberra the greatest per capita usage in Australia? No, but it's a sufficiently high usage rate that there's a marketplace," he said.
"And when there's a marketplace for cocaine, there's going to be a marketplace for bikies to be involved."
'Billions and billions'
This illicit economy is substantial; earlier this month, police arrested several ACT gang members alleged to have trafficked 70kg of cocaine with a street value of approximately $10 million.
"When you extrapolate that out to the [national] illicit drug market, we're talking billions and billions of dollars in terms of the illicit commodities that are moved into our country," Deputy Commissioner Lee said.
He explained the gangs had established transnational connections to overseas chapters in Europe, South America and other source regions.
Chapters are also constantly trying to recruit new members, particularly vulnerable young men seeking "status".
"They see outlaw motorcycle gangs as money and power," Sergeant Alexander said.
But police say except for OMCG top brass, most gang members take extreme risks for little reward.
"They are not making a lot of money. They are very poor. Sometimes they will struggle to pay the rent,"
Disrupting the cycle
New laws announced by the ACT government in February will give police more power to search for illegal firearms without needing a warrant.
Another change announced by the ACT government in March this year — just prior to a national Bandidos meeting in Canberra — was a ban on 'colours' or 'patches'.
"Colours are obviously worn to intimidate the community. They bring with it a connection to that OMCG,"
"It is something I've been supportive of with government, and I've advocated with government for the banning of colours here in the ACT."
Both proposals are yet to be debated in the ACT Legislative Assembly.
Constantly evolving
Whatever laws change, police say bikie gangs will adapt, adopting new tactics and strategies to keep business going.
"We are seeing a more underground meeting[s]… or it's in public areas, bars, clubs, restaurants, but they're not wearing their colours," Sergeant Mark Alexander said.
So, in the police's evolving fight against the gangs, they are clear one thing will never change: the need for public assistance.
"We can't be on every street corner keeping an eye on these people,"
"We rely on anonymous tips."
And Deputy Commissioner Lee urged the public to come forward.
"We need your help."

Q: I get headaches whenever I use my phone or computer for a long time. Are screens damaging my brain?
A: Screens are not known to damage the brain simply through use, but prolonged use can cause eye strain, dry eyes, blurred vision, neck and shoulder tension and headaches. Poor posture, glare and inadequate breaks can worsen symptoms. Follow the 20-20-20 rule: every 20 minutes, look about 20 feet away for 20 seconds. Adjust brightness, reduce glare and blink regularly. Frequent or severe headaches, especially without screen use, need medical evaluation.
Q: Is every headache a migraine?
A: No. Headaches can result from stress, tension, dehydration, poor sleep, eye strain, infections, sinus problems, stomach problems or migraine. Migraine may cause throbbing pain, nausea and sensitivity to light or sound, though symptoms vary. A new, unusually severe or rapidly worsening headache, especially with weakness, confusion, fainting, seizures, vision changes, fever or difficulty speaking, needs urgent medical attention.
Q: I have a headache, so I take a painkiller immediately. Is that okay?
A: Occasional appropriate use may be fine for some people, but frequent painkiller use can cause medication-overuse headaches and, depending on the medicine, stomach, kidney or liver problems. If you regularly need painkillers for headaches, find the cause rather than repeatedly treating the symptom.
Q: Do I really need a flu shot if I usually get only a mild flu?
A: Influenza can be mild but can also cause serious illness, especially in high-risk people. Flu vaccination reduces the risk of influenza and its complications, though it does not prevent every cold or respiratory virus. Because influenza viruses change, seasonal vaccination is recommended for many people according to individual risk. Ask your doctor if it is appropriate for you, particularly if you have chronic diseases, are pregnant or belong to another recommended group.
Q: Can the flu shot give me influenza?
A: No. Injectable flu vaccines do not contain live influenza virus capable of causing influenza. Soreness, tiredness or a mild fever can occur briefly after vaccination and usually reflect an immune response. You can also catch another respiratory virus around the same time. Remember that protection takes time to develop.
Q: My eyes burn after looking at my phone for hours. Do I need “screen glasses”?
A: Not necessarily. Digital eye strain can cause burning, dryness, temporary blurred vision and headaches because we blink less while concentrating. Take regular breaks, blink consciously, reduce glare and keep the screen at a comfortable distance. Prescription glasses may help if you have an underlying vision problem. Blue-light glasses are not a magic solution. Persistent pain or significant vision changes need an eye examination.
Q: Does using a phone in the dark permanently damage eyesight?
A: Ordinary phone use in a dark room has not been shown to permanently damage eyesight, although the bright screen against a dark background can cause strain, dryness or headaches. Keep some ambient light on and adjust screen brightness. Persistent blurred or double vision, eye pain or headaches should not simply be blamed on the phone.
Q: I use my phone until I fall asleep. Does it really affect sleep?
A: It does. Screen use keeps the brain engaged, while light from screens can affect the body’s sleep-wake rhythm. Messages, videos and social media can be particularly stimulating. Keep the phone away from the bed, choose quieter activities before sleep and maintain a regular bedtime. Persistent sleep problems need further evaluation.
Q: Can sitting in front of a screen all day cause neck and back pain?
A: Yes. Prolonged sitting and poor posture can cause neck, shoulder and back pain, while looking down at a phone can add neck strain. Change position regularly, keep the screen at a comfortable height, support your back and move around during the day. Exercise and strengthening can help. Persistent pain, numbness, weakness or pain spreading into an arm or leg should be assessed.
Q: I feel dizzy and get a headache after spending hours on my phone. Is it because of radiation?
A: There is no good evidence that ordinary mobile-phone use causes headaches or dizziness through the radiation emitted by phones. However, prolonged use can indirectly contribute through eye strain, poor posture, dehydration, lack of sleep and inactivity. Look at the whole pattern and take regular breaks. If headaches or dizziness keep returning, particularly without screen use, consult your doctor.
Q: Are “sugar-free” foods healthy?
A: No. “Sugar-free” does not mean nutritious. Sugar-free biscuits, chocolates and snacks may still be high in calories, refined flour, saturated fat or salt. Some contain sugar alcohols or other sweeteners that can cause gas, bloating or diarrhoea when consumed in excess. They may also keep our preference for very sweet foods alive. Sugar-free is a label, not a health certificate. Always check the complete nutrition label.
Q: Are zero-sugar drinks harmless?
A: Not necessarily. They can be a better choice than sugary drinks if you are trying to reduce sugar and calories, but they are not automatically healthy. Some sweeteners can cause gas, bloating, abdominal cramps or diarrhoea, particularly in people with sensitive digestion or IBS. If a particular drink repeatedly causes bowel discomfort, stop it and see whether symptoms improve. Zero sugar does not mean zero consequences.
Public Advisory: Not every health problem needs a tablet—and not every health myth deserves to be believed. From WhatsApp remedies and “natural” cures to advice from friends and relatives, health information can easily become distorted. Before starting, stopping or changing a treatment, ask the doctor—not the WhatsApp group.
NOTE: These responses are for general awareness and do not replace professional medical advice. Older adults often have multiple illnesses and medicines, so individual medical advice should be taken from a qualified healthcare professional.
